Report the open, closed and overdue action counts at the top of every committee pack so the committee sees its own follow-through.
Close an action only on the evidence stated when it was raised, not on an owner's assertion.
Carry actions overdue by more than one meeting cycle into the annual effectiveness assessment as a named weakness.
checklist.done: every minuted action is on the log with an owner and due date, is chased and escalated on slippage, and is closed only on stated evidence.

checklist.step: Report the governance position to the Board annually
actions: Prepare the annual ERISA governance report: named fiduciaries by plan, appointments and removals in the year, meetings held versus charter frequency, quorum failures, minute approval timeliness, delegations and their monitoring evidence, bond adequacy, and open governance issues.
State plainly any period in which a plan had no validly appointed fiduciary or acted without quorum, and what was done about it.
Ask General Counsel to append a legal opinion on the validity of any ratification the Board is being asked to make.
Load the report to the board portal 5 business days before the meeting and minute the Board's acceptance and any decisions.
Publish the accepted report into the compliance evidence repository as the year's governance evidence pack.
checklist.done: the annual governance report is tabled with 5 business days' notice, states every authority gap, and the Board's acceptance is minuted.

checklist.step: Retain the governance record for the ERISA period
actions: Export from the board portal each year's charters, agendas, packs, approved minutes and resolutions to the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Governance / <plan year>.
Export from iManage the appointment and acceptance letters, delegation instruments and fidelity bond with its calculation.
Apply the 6-year ERISA §107 label to routine governance records and the indefinite label to any minute or resolution that changed a benefit, a plan term or a participant entitlement, per ERISA §209.
Index the pack so it is retrievable by plan number, committee and plan year for an EBSA investigator or the plan's independent auditor.
Confirm the board portal version history remains intact and unalterable for the retained period, and record the ingestion date.
checklist.done: each year's governance pack is in the repository with the correct ERISA labels, indexed by plan, committee and year, with portal version history intact.

testing.step: Build the population of meetings, appointments and delegations
actions: Extract from the board portal every ERISA committee and board meeting held in the period with date, committee, attendees and the minute status.
Extract the fiduciary register, the delegation register and the bond schedule as at period end.
Reconcile meetings held to the charter's required frequency and to the twelve-month calendar, and list any sitting that was cancelled and never rescheduled.
Reconcile the fiduciary register to the plan-document schedule of named fiduciaries and to HRIS leaver data so a departed fiduciary cannot still be on the register.
Sign the population as complete with the extract queries, run date and row counts.
testing.done: the meeting, appointment, delegation and bond populations reconcile to the charters, plan documents and HRIS leaver data and are signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile named fiduciaries to the operative plan documents
actions: Open each plan document and adoption agreement in iManage and read the fiduciary article yourself rather than relying on the schedule.
Confirm every plan names a fiduciary under ERISA §402(a)(1) and contains the §402(b)(2) allocation procedure; a plan with neither is an immediate Critical exception.
Confirm the person or committee actually deciding appeals is the one the plan document and the SPD name, and that the SPD description matches the procedure in operation per 29 CFR 2560.503-1(b).
Flag any fiduciary acting under a defunct job title or an unconstituted committee as acting without authority.
testing.done: every plan is confirmed to name a fiduciary and an allocation procedure, and the acting appeals decider matches the plan document and SPD, or an exception is raised.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of meetings and appointments
actions: Take 100% of meetings at which a benefit-affecting or investment decision was recorded, and 100% of appointments and removals in the period.
Take 10 further meetings by seeded random selection across both committees, and 10 delegation instruments weighted to the largest plans by assets.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample re-draws identically.
Confirm no sampled meeting was minuted by, and no sampled appointment processed by, the auditor performing the test.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible with full coverage of decision meetings, appointments and removals.

testing.step: Recompute quorum and authority on every sampled decision
actions: For each sampled decision, count the members present from the attendance register — excluding attendees and invitees — and compare to the quorum in the charter edition in force on the meeting date.
Check each member present held a live appointment on that date, with an acceptance letter dated before the meeting and no removal date before it.
Confirm the decision fell inside the committee's charter decision rights and was not a matter reserved to the Board.
Treat any decision taken inquorate, by a member without a live acceptance, or outside charter authority as a Critical exception and an unauthorised fiduciary act.
testing.done: each sampled decision has a recomputed quorum, member-by-member authority check and a charter-authority test, with failures rated Critical.

testing.step: Test minute content against the prudence evidence standard
actions: Open the approved minutes for each sampled decision and mark, as separate attributes, whether the question, the options considered, the data or advice relied on with its paper reference, the discussion, any dissent, the resolution and the vote are each recorded.
Trace the advice relied on to the actual paper in the meeting pack and confirm it pre-dates the meeting and was uploaded before the cut-off.
Recompute the drafting interval (draft date − meeting date) against the 10-business-day standard and the approval interval against the one-meeting-cycle standard.
Treat a minute that records only the resolution, with no options or advice, as failing the ERISA §404(a)(1)(B) evidence standard even where the decision itself was sound.
testing.done: each sampled decision's minute is scored attribute by attribute, its advice traced to a pre-meeting paper, and its drafting and approval intervals recomputed.

testing.step: Trace delegations to executed instruments and actual monitoring
actions: Open each sampled delegation instrument in iManage and confirm it is executed, names the scope, the performance standard, the reporting owed and the monitoring the fiduciary will do.
Pull the monitoring reports the instrument requires for the period and confirm they were actually produced and tabled at a committee meeting, tracing to a minute reference.
For any ERISA §3(38) investment manager, confirm the written acknowledgement of fiduciary status is on file and current.
Treat a delegation with no monitoring evidence as an ERISA §405(c)(2) co-fiduciary exposure and report it to the Committee, not as a filing gap.
testing.done: every sampled delegation is executed with a monitoring obligation and traced to monitoring reports actually tabled at a minuted meeting.

testing.step: Recompute the fidelity bond adequacy for every plan
actions: Recompute the required bond as 10% of funds handled in the preceding plan year from the trust financial statements, applying the $1,000 floor, the $500,000 cap and the $1,000,000 cap where employer securities are held.
Compare to the bond in force and confirm the plan is a named insured, the surety appears on the Treasury Department Circular 570 list, and no deductible applies to the plan.
Check the policy period covers the full plan year with no gap at renewal and that any mid-year increase in funds handled was reflected within 30 days.
Compare the recomputed figures to the Form 5500 Schedule H line 4e or Schedule I bonding answer and treat any inconsistency as a filing exception as well as a bonding one.
testing.done: each plan's bond is recomputed against trust financials and tied to the Form 5500 bonding answer, with surety listing and no-deductible confirmed.

testing.step: Test the ERISA §209 participant record completeness
actions: Select 25 participants spanning long-service, terminated-vested and recently converted-recordkeeper populations.
Reconcile the recordkeeper's service and compensation history for each to payroll source data year by year and list every missing or conflicting year.
For participants who came across a recordkeeper conversion, confirm the pre-conversion history was actually loaded and not merely archived at the prior provider.
Confirm beneficiary designations and service records carry the indefinite retention label rather than a 6-year label that would destroy them.
Treat any participant whose benefit could not be computed from the records held as a Critical ERISA §209 exception.
testing.done: each tested participant's service and compensation history reconciles to payroll across conversions, or is raised as a Critical §209 exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the plan, committee, meeting or instrument reference and the fiduciary consequence stated.

Assign a root cause — appointment lapsed at a leaver event, quorum not tested before the vote, minute drafted from a template rather than the discussion, delegation never papered, bond not re-sized, conversion history not loaded — and a named owner.
Set 30 days for authority and bonding exceptions and 90 days for record and process changes, with the closure evidence stated at the point of raising.
Refer every unauthorised fiduciary act to General Counsel for a ratification opinion and, where plan assets were affected, an EBSA Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a root cause, a named owner, a dated remediation and, for authority failures, a counsel ratification referral.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute minute approval attainment against the 95% threshold and count the zero-tolerance failures — plans without a named fiduciary, inquorate decisions, fiduciaries acting without acceptance, and under-sized or lapsed bonds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind every figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the Corporate Secretariat and minuted none of the sampled meetings, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the exception schedule and every unauthorised fiduciary act to the Board and the ERISA Plan Administration Committee at their next sittings.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Governance / <period> with the ERISA §107 retention label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating minute-approval attainment, zero-tolerance failures, a conclusion and Board reporting dates is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the governance disclosure calendar spanning the ERISA Form 5500 series filed through EFAST2 for every administered plan, the Summary Annual Report, PBGC premium and Form 4010 filings for covered defined benefit plans, and the insurer-side NAIC Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure and Form B/Form F holding-company filings that describe the same fiduciary governance structure.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — ERISA §103 and §104 annual reporting with the current-year Form 5500 instructions on efast.dol.gov, 29 CFR 2520.104b-10 for the SAR, 29 CFR 2578.1 for abandoned-plan terminations and final filings, plus the lead state's Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure statute and the NAIC Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act Form B and Form F instructions, each re-read at the start of the filing season.

In-scope processes.value: Annual report assembly and certification for every ERISA plan — participant counts, Schedules A, C, D, H or I, SB or MB, the independent qualified public accountant report for large plans — plus SAR production and distribution, PBGC premium determination, and the CGAD and holding-company governance narrative describing the same board and committee structure.

In-scope systems.value: Filing calendar, preparer/reviewer/signer workflow and submission receipts held in the Internal Regulatory System; Form 5500 assembled and transmitted through the EFAST2 electronic filing system; CGAD and Form B/Form F narratives drafted in the board portal from approved charters and minutes; trust and plan financials from the ERP/General ledger.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Governance and Annual Reporting Filing Procedure — the per-plan filing matrix, data sources for each schedule, the large/small plan and 80-120 participant-count rule, audit engagement timing, the electronic signature and credential rules for EFAST2, extension policy, and the CGAD/Form B narrative source-of-truth rule that governance text is drawn from approved charters and minutes only.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and General Counsel; the CGAD content is approved by the Board or the designated board committee each year before filing, and the whole procedure is re-approved annually and on any change to the Form 5500 instructions or a state CGAD statute.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form 5500 due the last day of the 7th month after plan year end (31 July for a calendar plan), extended to the 15th day of the 10th month (15 October) on a timely Form 5558; SAR to participants within 9 months of plan year end, or 2 months after the extended Form 5500 is filed; PBGC comprehensive premium filing by 15 October for calendar-year plans and Form 4010 within 105 days of the information date; CGAD to the lead state by 1 June; Form B annual registration by the state's date (commonly 30 April) and within 15 days of a change of control event.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Internal Regulatory System milestone alerts at T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-10 days against each filing due date, with a hard alert to the Corporate Secretary and Controller at T-45 on any plan whose independent auditor has not yet issued, since the audit report is the usual cause of a late Form 5500.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed Form 5500 with all schedules and attachments, the EFAST2 acknowledgement id and filing receipt, the signer credential record, the auditor's report and management representation letter, the SAR specimen with distribution proof, and the board-approved CGAD, retained 6 years from filing per ERISA §107 and per the lead state's CGAD record rule.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late filings, rejected EFAST2 submissions, unsigned or wrongly signed returns, missing IQPA reports and CGAD content that diverges from the approved charters are logged with root cause, the correction route (Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program or an amended filing) and the resubmission date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every amended or delinquent filing, approves entry into the DOL Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program, and clears any CGAD or Form B narrative correction before it goes to the lead state.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every ERISA plan required to file a Form 5500 or 5500-SF for the plan year, every SAR owed, every PBGC premium and 4010 filing, and the CGAD and Form B/Form F filings made in the year, across all filing entities and lead states.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on lateness — any Form 5500 filed after its due date or valid extension, any SAR distributed after 9 months, or any CGAD filed after 1 June is a fail; zero tolerance on an unfiled IQPA report for a large plan; any CGAD statement that cannot be traced to an approved charter or minute is a content fail escalated to the Board.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with event-driven holding-company triggers; the test runs once per filing season over the full population after the 15 October extended deadline, with an event-driven test within 30 days of any change-of-control Form B filing.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared, reviewed or signed any filing in the population and must sit outside the Corporate Secretariat and Regulatory Reporting.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual governance filing test workpaper — filing matrix, EFAST2 acknowledgement trace, schedule-to-ledger reconciliations, SAR distribution proof, deadline recomputation and the CGAD source trace — filed in the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Filings / <plan year>.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-plan filing pack — the filed return with schedules, the EFAST2 acknowledgement id, the IQPA report, the SAR specimen and distribution proof, and the board-approved CGAD with the minute approving it — producible to EBSA, PBGC or the lead state within 10 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers EFAST2 and PBGC correspondence; the Corporate Secretary answers lead-state CGAD questions; General Counsel is the single channel for any DOL notice of late filing and decides on Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program entry before any reply is sent.

checklist.step: Build the filing matrix for the plan year
actions: List every ERISA plan with its three-digit plan number, sponsor EIN, plan year end, plan type and funding arrangement.
Determine the return for each: Form 5500, Form 5500-SF for eligible small plans, or Form 5500-EZ where no ERISA filing is owed, and record the basis for the choice.

Apply the participant-count rule at the first day of the plan year and the 80-120 rule that lets a plan between 80 and 120 participants keep its prior year's large or small filing status, and record the count and the decision.

For each plan list the schedules owed — A for insurance contracts, C for service provider compensation on large plans, D for CCT/PSA/MTIA interests, H or I for financials, SB or MB for defined benefit funding, R for retirement distributions.
Load the matrix into the Internal Regulatory System with the due date, the extended date and the named preparer, reviewer and signer for each plan.
checklist.done: every plan has a matrix row with return type, participant count, status decision, schedules owed, due and extended dates and named preparer, reviewer and signer.

checklist.step: Engage the independent qualified public accountant early enough to file on time
actions: Engage the IQPA for every large plan by the end of the second month after plan year end, since ERISA §103(a)(3)(A) requires the audit report to be attached to the Form 5500.
Agree an engagement timetable that puts the signed opinion in hand at least 45 days before the filing due date, and put that date in the engagement letter.

Confirm the auditor's independence under DOL rules and that the engagement is a full-scope audit unless a valid 29 CFR 2520.103-8 limited-scope certification from a qualifying institution is in place.
Where limited scope is used, obtain the trustee or custodian certification and confirm it covers all certified investment information and is signed by an authorised officer.
Escalate to the Corporate Secretary at T-45 any plan whose opinion is not issued, because that is the point at which the extension decision must be taken.
checklist.done: each large plan has an engaged IQPA, a timetable delivering the opinion 45 days before due, and a valid certification where limited scope is used.

checklist.step: Assemble the financial schedules from the ledger and trust records
actions: Pull the plan's statement of net assets and statement of changes from the trustee's year-end report and reconcile it to the plan's ledger account in the ERP before any schedule is populated.
Populate Schedule H assets and liabilities, income and expenses lines from the reconciled trial balance and tie the total net assets to the trustee statement to the dollar.

Populate Schedule H line 4 compliance questions deliberately — party-in-interest transactions, delinquent participant contributions, fidelity bond amount, and the accountant's opinion type — and evidence each answer.

Where participant contributions were remitted after the earliest date they could reasonably be segregated, report them on line 4a and start the prohibited-transaction correction with lost earnings, rather than answering no.
File the reconciliation as the working paper behind the schedule so a reviewer can retrace every figure.
checklist.done: each financial schedule ties to the reconciled trustee statement and trial balance, with line 4 answers individually evidenced.

checklist.step: Collect service provider compensation for Schedule C
actions: List every service provider paid $5,000 or more directly or indirectly from plan assets during the plan year from the vendor master and the trust disbursement report.
Request from each provider its written statement of direct and indirect compensation for the plan year, referencing their ERISA §408(b)(2) disclosure obligation, and give a 30-day response window.
Identify eligible indirect compensation and confirm the alternative reporting conditions are met — the disclosures the provider gave the fiduciary must be adequate — before treating it as eligible.
Report on Schedule C Part I any provider that failed or refused to supply the information, since that reporting is itself required.
Give the Regulatory Reporting Manager the schedule with each provider's EIN, service codes and compensation amounts.
checklist.done: every $5,000-plus provider has a written compensation statement or is reported as non-responsive, with service codes and EINs supplied.

checklist.step: Draft the governance narrative from approved charters and minutes only
actions: Draft the CGAD sections required by the lead state's statute: the corporate governance framework and structure, board and committee composition and qualifications, board and management policies and practices for directing the insurer, and the policies on management succession and compensation.

Draw every factual statement from the board portal record — the approved charter edition, the membership register and the minutes — and footnote each statement to its source document so nothing is written from memory.

Describe the ERISA plan committee structure consistently with the charters filed in the governance pack; a CGAD that describes a committee the charters do not create is a misstatement to the regulator.
Prepare the Form B annual registration and Form F enterprise risk report from the same source set, and confirm the organisational chart matches the current legal entity register.
Circulate the draft to General Counsel for legal review and record the review comments and their disposition.
checklist.done: every CGAD, Form B and Form F statement is footnoted to an approved charter, register or minute, and General Counsel's review is recorded.

checklist.step: Take the governance disclosure to the Board for approval
actions: Table the CGAD to the Board or the designated board committee at least 5 business days ahead, with the footnoted source references attached.
Ask the Board to approve the content and to authorise the signing officer, because most CGAD statutes require the filing to be signed by a designated officer attesting the disclosure was approved.
Minute the approval, the officer authorised and any changes the Board directed, and confirm those changes are made before filing.
Where the Board directs a governance change in the same meeting, decide explicitly whether the CGAD describes the position as at the reporting date or as amended, and record which.
Publish the approved final to the board portal as the filed version of record.
checklist.done: the Board has approved the CGAD content and named the signing officer, with the approval and any directed changes minuted before filing.

checklist.step: Run the preparer, reviewer and signer workflow before transmission
actions: Route the assembled return through the Internal Regulatory System workflow: preparer completes, reviewer signs off each schedule against its working paper, then the plan administrator signs.
Run the reviewer checklist covering participant counts, EIN and plan number consistency with prior year, schedule attachment completeness, the IQPA report attachment and the fidelity bond answer.
Confirm the plan administrator holds valid EFAST2 filing signer credentials and that the credentials belong to the individual signing, not a shared account — EFAST2 signatures are personal.
Compare every carried-forward figure to the prior year filing and investigate any unexplained movement above a defined threshold before signing.
Record the preparer, reviewer, signer and their dates on the filing record.
checklist.done: each return carries a completed reviewer checklist, a prior-year comparison, and named preparer, reviewer and signer with dates and personal EFAST2 credentials.

checklist.step: Transmit through EFAST2 and capture the acknowledgement
actions: Transmit the return through EFAST2 using IFILE or the approved third-party software and wait for the filing status to move past Processing.
Record the EFAST2 acknowledgement id, the submission date and time, and the filing status on the filing record.
Where the status returns Filing Error or Unprocessable, read the error detail, correct and resubmit the same business day — an unprocessed submission is not a filing.
Retrieve the filed return as accepted from EFAST2 rather than keeping only the locally assembled copy, since the accepted version is what the regulator holds.
Confirm the filing appears on the EFAST2 filing search for the plan and sponsor within the expected publication window.
checklist.done: every return shows an EFAST2 acknowledgement id, an accepted status, and the accepted copy retrieved and filed.

checklist.step: Take the extension deliberately where the audit will not land
actions: At T-45 review every plan without a signed IQPA opinion or a reconciled schedule set with the Controller.
Where the original due date is not achievable, file Form 5558 with the IRS on or before the original due date — a Form 5558 filed one day late gives no extension at all.
Record the Form 5558 filing date and proof on the filing record and reset the plan's milestone alerts to the extended 15 October date.
Recompute the SAR deadline for extended plans as 2 months after the Form 5500 is actually filed and reissue the SAR schedule accordingly.
Escalate to General Counsel any plan that will miss even the extended date so the Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program route is assessed before, not after, the deadline passes.
checklist.done: every plan needing more time has a Form 5558 filed on or before the original due date, with milestone alerts and SAR dates reset.

checklist.step: Produce and distribute the Summary Annual Report
actions: Generate the SAR for each plan from the filed Form 5500 figures using the prescribed format in 29 CFR 2520.104b-10, including the statement of the participant's right to receive a copy of the full annual report.
Reconcile every figure in the SAR to the filed Schedule H or I line it comes from, and have a second preparer initial the reconciliation.
Distribute within 9 months of plan year end, or within 2 months after the extended Form 5500 was filed, to all participants and beneficiaries receiving benefits.
Use the address of record and, where electronic delivery is used, confirm the 29 CFR 2520.104b-31 conditions are satisfied.
Capture the print vendor mail-date file or the electronic delivery receipts as distribution proof and file them against the plan.
checklist.done: each plan's SAR ties figure by figure to the filed return and is distributed inside the 9-month or 2-month window with delivery proof captured.

checklist.step: Complete the PBGC filings for covered defined benefit plans
actions: Identify every PBGC-covered defined benefit plan, including any plan taken on through a pension risk transfer transaction in the year.

Compute the flat-rate premium on the participant count at the prior year end and the variable-rate premium on unfunded vested benefits, applying the current year premium rates and the variable-rate cap.
File the comprehensive premium filing through PBGC My PAA by 15 October for a calendar-year plan and capture the filing confirmation and payment reference.
Where the controlled group meets the Form 4010 reporting trigger, file within 105 days of the information date with the actuarial and financial information the regulation requires.
Report any reportable event under ERISA §4043 within its own deadline — commonly 30 days — rather than folding it into the annual filing.
checklist.done: each covered plan has a My PAA premium filing with a confirmation and payment reference, and any Form 4010 or §4043 event is filed on its own clock.

checklist.step: File the CGAD and holding-company forms with the lead state
actions: Submit the board-approved CGAD to the lead state by 1 June through the channel that state requires, signed by the officer the Board authorised.
Submit the Form B annual registration statement by the state's due date and any Form F enterprise risk report the lead state requires alongside it.

Where a change of control, a new affiliate or a material transaction occurred, file the amended Form B within 15 days after the end of the month in which the event happened rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Request and file the state's confidentiality acknowledgement, since CGAD content is confidential by statute and mishandling it is itself a breach.
Record the submission date, the receiving state, the confirmation reference and the signing officer on the filing record.
checklist.done: the CGAD is filed by 1 June and the holding-company forms by their state dates, each with a confirmation reference and the confidentiality acknowledgement on file.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed population to the plan inventory
actions: After the extended deadline, list every plan on the inventory against its filing record and confirm each has an accepted EFAST2 acknowledgement or a documented reason it owed no return.
Search the EFAST2 public filing database by sponsor EIN and confirm the filings appear there, since an internal record is not proof the regulator received it.

Confirm terminated plans filed a final return with the final-return box checked and that any abandoned plan followed the 29 CFR 2578.1 qualified termination administrator process and its special terminal report.
List any plan with no accepted filing as a delinquency the same day and open the correction route.
Publish the reconciliation to the Chief Financial Officer and General Counsel.
checklist.done: every plan on the inventory ties to an accepted EFAST2 filing visible in the public database or a documented no-filing basis, and delinquencies are opened same day.

checklist.step: Correct late or defective filings through the right programme
actions: For any unfiled or late Form 5500, assess the Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program before the DOL issues a notice, since the reduced penalty is only available if the plan comes forward first.
Prepare and submit the delinquent return through EFAST2 with the DFVCP box completed, then pay the applicable per-plan penalty through the DFVCP online calculator and payment system.
For a filed but wrong return, submit an amended Form 5500 with the amended box checked and a statement of what changed and why.

Where the error is a delinquent participant contribution, run the Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program correction with lost earnings computed on the DOL online calculator, and keep the calculator output.
Record the programme used, the payment reference and the closure date on the filing issue tracker.
checklist.done: each late or defective filing is corrected through DFVCP, an amended return or VFCP, with the payment reference and closure date recorded.

checklist.step: Retain the complete filing pack for the retention period
actions: Assemble per plan: the accepted return with all schedules and attachments, the EFAST2 acknowledgement id and receipt, the IQPA report and representation letter, the schedule working papers, the SAR specimen and distribution proof, and any Form 5558.
Assemble per entity: the board-approved CGAD with the approving minute, the Form B and Form F submissions and the state confirmations and confidentiality acknowledgements.
File both into the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Filings / <plan year> and apply the 6-year ERISA §107 retention label from the filing date.
Index by plan number, sponsor EIN, form type and plan year so an EBSA or lead-state request can be answered inside 10 business days.
Apply a legal hold where a DOL investigation, PBGC enquiry or state examination touching the entity is open.
checklist.done: per-plan and per-entity filing packs are in the repository with the 6-year label, indexed by plan number, EIN, form type and year.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of filings owed for the plan year
actions: Extract the plan inventory from the recordkeeping and legal entity registers independently of the filing matrix and compare plan counts.
Confirm every plan that existed for any part of the plan year is in the population, including plans terminated mid-year that still owe a final return.
Add the entity-level CGAD, Form B and Form F obligations by lead state and the PBGC-covered plan list from the actuarial valuation file.
Investigate every difference against the filing matrix before sampling — a plan missing from the matrix never gets a deadline and is the classic delinquency.
Sign the population as complete with the extract queries, run date and counts.
testing.done: the independently rebuilt population agrees to the filing matrix plan by plan and entity by entity, with every difference explained.

testing.step: Reconcile every filing to the regulator's own record
actions: Search the EFAST2 public filing database by sponsor EIN and plan number for each population plan and record the acknowledgement id and received date shown there.
Compare the regulator's received date to the internal filing record and to the plan's due or extended date and recompute the days difference.
Confirm each PBGC premium filing appears in My PAA with a confirmation number and that payment cleared, and confirm the CGAD and Form B carry a state confirmation reference.
Treat any filing present internally but absent from the regulator's record as unfiled, regardless of the internal status, and raise it as a Critical exception.
testing.done: every filing is traced to the regulator's own record with its received date recomputed against the due date, or raised as unfiled.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across plans and entities
actions: Take 100% of large plans requiring an IQPA report, 100% of extended filings, 100% of PBGC-covered plans and 100% of CGAD and Form B filings.
Take 15 small-plan filings by seeded random selection and 15 SAR distributions across plan types.
Record the seed, population size, stratum counts and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm no sampled filing was prepared, reviewed or signed by the auditor performing the test.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible with full coverage of large plans, extensions, PBGC plans and governance filings.

testing.step: Recompute due dates, extensions and the SAR clock
actions: Recompute each plan's due date as the last day of the 7th month after plan year end from the plan document's plan year end, not the filing matrix field.
Where an extension was used, open the Form 5558 and confirm it was filed on or before the original due date, then recompute the extended date as the 15th day of the 10th month.
Recompute the SAR deadline as 9 months after plan year end, or 2 months after the actual Form 5500 filing date for extended plans, and compare to the distribution mail date on the vendor file.
Recompute the PBGC premium due date and the Form 4010 105-day clock from the information date.
Treat a Form 5558 filed after the original due date as no extension at all, making the return late from the original date.
testing.done: every sampled deadline is recomputed from source plan-year and filing dates, with extension validity separately proved.

testing.step: Trace financial schedules back to trust and ledger source
actions: For 10 sampled plans, agree Schedule H total net assets at year end to the trustee's year-end statement and to the plan ledger balance in the ERP, to the dollar.
Agree contributions received to the payroll remittance file and benefit payments to the disbursement register.
Re-read Schedule H line 4a on delinquent participant contributions and test it against the remittance-date analysis rather than accepting the reported answer.
Confirm the fidelity bond amount reported agrees to the bond in force and to the ERISA §412 recomputation.
List every unreconciled difference as an exception with both figures shown.
testing.done: each sampled plan's schedule figures tie to trustee statements, ledger balances and remittance and disbursement records, or differences are listed.

testing.step: Verify the IQPA report and the limited-scope basis
actions: Confirm every large plan's filing has the IQPA report attached in the accepted EFAST2 submission, not merely on the internal file.
Read the opinion type and confirm the Schedule H line reporting it matches — a disclaimer reported as unmodified is a filing misstatement.

Where a limited-scope certification was relied on, obtain the certification and confirm it is signed by an authorised officer of a qualifying bank or insurance carrier and covers all the investment information excluded from the audit.
Confirm the auditor's independence representation is on file and that the engagement letter date precedes fieldwork.
testing.done: each large plan's accepted filing carries an IQPA report whose opinion type matches the schedule, with any limited-scope certification validated.

testing.step: Trace every CGAD statement to an approved governance source
actions: Take 20 factual statements from the filed CGAD about board composition, committee remit, meeting frequency and management oversight.
Trace each to its footnoted source in the board portal — the charter edition in force, the membership register or the approved minute — and confirm the source actually says it.
Confirm the committee structure described matches the ERISA plan committee charters filed in the governance pack, since the same structure is described to two regulators.
Confirm the Board approved the content and authorised the signing officer, and that the officer who signed is the one named in the minute.
Treat any statement with no traceable source as a misstatement to the regulator and escalate it to the Board, not as a drafting observation.
testing.done: every traced CGAD statement resolves to an approved charter, register or minute, and the signing officer matches the authorising minute.

testing.step: Test SAR content and distribution proof
actions: Agree each sampled SAR's figures line by line to the Schedule H or I lines of the filed return.
Confirm the prescribed 29 CFR 2520.104b-10 format elements are present, including the participant's right to receive the full annual report on request.
Trace the distribution to the print vendor mail-date file or electronic delivery receipts and compare the mail date to the recomputed deadline.
Confirm the distribution population equals the participants and beneficiaries receiving benefits at the relevant date, and investigate any shortfall against the recordkeeper's headcount.
testing.done: each sampled SAR ties to the filed return, carries the prescribed format elements, and its distribution date and population are proved from vendor and recordkeeper data.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and correction route
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the plan or entity, form type, deadline, actual date and the days late or the misstated figure.
Assign a root cause — plan absent from the matrix, audit late, Form 5558 filed late, schedule not reconciled, signer credential invalid, CGAD statement unsourced — and a named owner.

State the correction route on the issue: DFVCP for a delinquent return, amended Form 5500 for a wrong one, VFCP with the DOL lost-earnings calculator for late contributions, or a corrected CGAD to the lead state.
Set 30 days for correction of any late or unfiled item and require the payment or confirmation reference as closure evidence.
Carry every open issue into the next filing season's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries a tracker issue with root cause, owner, a named correction programme and a confirmation reference as closure evidence.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Count the zero-tolerance failures — Form 5500s filed after the due or extended date, SARs distributed beyond the window, CGADs filed after 1 June, large plans missing an IQPA report, and unsourced CGAD statements.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind every figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, reviewed and signed none of the population and sits outside Corporate Secretariat and Regulatory Reporting, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, the exception schedule and any delinquency correction to the Audit Committee, the ERISA Plan Administration Committee and the Board.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Filings / <plan year> with the 6-year ERISA §107 label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper counting zero-tolerance failures, stating a conclusion and recording committee reporting dates is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the fitness-and-propriety assessment run at every appointment to an ERISA fiduciary, plan officer, trustee or plan-asset-handling role, jointly with the HR Business Partner who runs the screening mechanics; the ERISA §411 disqualification determination itself is a legal call and cannot be delegated to Recruiting.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — ERISA §411 (29 U.S.C. §1111) thirteen-year bar on service by persons convicted of the listed offences, ERISA §412 with 29 CFR 2580 bonding of every person who handles plan funds, ERISA §404(a)(1)(B) prudence in selecting the persons who carry out fiduciary functions, and the Fair Credit Reporting Act disclosure and adverse-action rules governing the background report, re-read at each annual procedure review.

In-scope processes.value: Appointment, promotion and transfer into any ERISA fiduciary or plan-asset-handling role — plan committee member, plan administrator, trustee, appeals decider, benefit payment approver, contribution remitter — plus director appointments and the annual re-attestation of every incumbent, and the equivalent assessment applied to key service provider personnel.

In-scope systems.value: Role-to-fiduciary mapping and appointment workflow in the HRIS with a mandatory pre-appointment screening gate; screening ordered through Credit Bureau & Data Services with public-record and sanctions checks supplemented from LexisNexis Risk; signed attestations and the legal determination memo filed in iManage (Legal Docs).

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Fitness and Propriety Assessment Procedure — which roles are in scope and why, the pre-appointment screening pack, the §411 offence list mapped to search terms, the FCRA disclosure and authorisation sequence, the pre-adverse and adverse action steps, the legal determination and appointment-blocking rules, and the annual re-attestation cycle.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief HR Officer and General Counsel and noted by the ERISA Plan Administration Committee; re-approved annually and out of cycle on any amendment to ERISA §411, a change of screening vendor, or a change in state law restricting criminal-history inquiries.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per appointment: screening ordered within 2 business days of the offer or nomination, the vendor report returned within 10 business days, the legal determination made within 3 business days of the report, and the appointment resolution passed only after the determination — no fiduciary act may precede it; incumbents re-attest annually within 30 days of the request and the fidelity bond schedule is updated within 30 days of any new plan-asset handler.

Deadline reminders configured.value: HRIS workflow blocks the appointment task until the screening result is attached, with reminders to the HR Business Partner at day 5 and day 8 of the vendor window and escalation to Employment Counsel at day 12; annual re-attestation campaigns launch 45 days before the plan year end with reminders at 30, 14 and 3 days.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Screening authorisation, the vendor report, the §411 determination memo, the signed attestation and the appointment resolution retained 6 years from the end of the appointment per ERISA §107, with access restricted to Employment Counsel and the HR Business Partner because the file contains criminal-history and consumer-report data.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Appointments made before a determination, missing or expired attestations, unscreened plan-asset handlers and any person identified as §411-barred are logged as issues with immediate removal action, a named owner and a closure date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Personally signs every §411 disqualification determination and every decision to remove or to retain an individual after an adverse finding, and confirms in writing whether acts taken by an improperly appointed person require ratification.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All appointments, promotions and transfers into ERISA fiduciary or plan-asset-handling roles in the period, all director appointments, the full incumbent population subject to annual re-attestation, and the key service provider personnel the plan relies on.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any person acting in a fiduciary or plan-asset-handling role with no completed pre-appointment determination is a fail, as is any §411-barred person in any covered role or covered by the fidelity bond; annual re-attestation completion must reach 100% of incumbents by plan year end.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per appointment; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's appointments with a full annual reconciliation of the incumbent fiduciary population to completed determinations and attestations.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside HR and Legal, must not have processed any sampled appointment, and works from redacted extracts where full consumer-report content is not needed.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly fitness-and-propriety test workpaper — appointment population, sample with seed, determination-date recomputation, attestation reconciliation and exception schedule — in the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Fitness and Propriety / <quarter>, with personal data referenced by employee id only.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-appointment pack — role-to-fiduciary mapping, screening authorisation, vendor report summary, the signed §411 determination, the attestation and the appointment resolution — producible to an EBSA investigator or a state insurance examiner within 10 business days under a confidentiality request.

Regulator response path.value: General Counsel is the single channel for any EBSA enquiry about a fiduciary's eligibility and decides on self-reporting where a §411-barred person is found to have served; the Corporate Secretary handles state biographical-affidavit follow-ups for officers and directors.

checklist.step: Map which roles are ERISA fiduciary or plan-asset-handling
actions: Work from the fiduciary register, the delegation register and the plan documents to list every position that exercises discretionary authority over plan management, plan assets or plan administration, since ERISA fiduciary status follows function not title.

Add every position that handles plan funds or other property for ERISA §412 bonding purposes — benefit payment approvers, contribution remitters, trust wire authorisers, and anyone with physical or signature access to plan assets.
Add director and officer positions caught by the ERISA §411 bar on serving as an administrator, fiduciary, officer, trustee, custodian, counsel, agent, employee or consultant of a plan.
Tag each mapped position in the HRIS with an ERISA-FIDUCIARY or ERISA-FUNDS-HANDLER flag so the appointment workflow can gate on it.
Review the map with the Chief HR Officer twice a year and after any reorganisation, because an untagged role is a role that never gets screened.
checklist.done: every discretionary and funds-handling position is tagged in the HRIS with an ERISA flag traceable to a plan document, register or bonding requirement.

checklist.step: Gate the appointment workflow on a completed assessment
actions: Configure the HRIS hire, promotion and transfer workflows so a move into an ERISA-flagged position cannot progress past offer approval without a Fitness and Propriety task marked Complete.
Make the gate apply to internal moves and secondments as well as external hires, since most fiduciary appointments are internal promotions.
Route the task to the HR Business Partner for screening and to Employment Counsel for determination, with both signatures required.
Configure the workflow to notify the Corporate Secretary when the gate clears, so the appointment resolution can be scheduled.
Test the gate quarterly with a dummy requisition and confirm it actually blocks rather than warns.
checklist.done: no ERISA-flagged appointment can be completed in the HRIS without a signed screening and determination task, proved by a quarterly gate test.

checklist.step: Obtain FCRA-compliant disclosure and authorisation before screening
actions: Issue the standalone written disclosure that a consumer report may be obtained for employment purposes — on its own document, with no liability waiver or other text on it, as the Fair Credit Reporting Act requires.

Obtain the candidate's written authorisation and, where the report will be an investigative consumer report, give the additional notice of the right to request the nature and scope of the investigation.
Capture the candidate's identifiers needed for a reliable search — full legal name, former names, date of birth and jurisdictions of residence for the last seven to thirteen years.
Check the state and locality rules that apply to the role's work location for ban-the-box or criminal-history timing restrictions and adjust the sequence rather than the substance.
File the signed disclosure and authorisation in iManage against the appointment before any search is ordered.
checklist.done: a standalone FCRA disclosure and a signed authorisation are on file, with jurisdictional timing rules applied, before any search is run.

checklist.step: Order the screening pack from the vendor
actions: Order the pack: county, state and federal criminal record searches across the jurisdictions of residence, national criminal database, sex offender registry, employment and education verification, professional licence verification and a global sanctions and PEP screen.

Add a federal court search specifically, because ERISA §411 offences such as mail fraud, wire fraud, embezzlement from a plan and violations of ERISA itself are typically federal and are missed by county-only searches.
For finance, treasury and trust-authority roles add a credit report only where the role justifies it and the jurisdiction permits it, and record the justification.
Set the vendor service level at 10 business days and track the order in the HRIS task.
Supplement with a LexisNexis Risk public-record and adverse-media search for director and officer appointments.
checklist.done: a screening order covering federal, state and county criminal records, sanctions and verifications is placed with a 10-business-day service level and tracked on the appointment task.

checklist.step: Take the candidate's own signed attestation
actions: Send the ERISA Fitness and Propriety attestation through DocuSign asking the candidate to confirm, on their own knowledge, that they have not been convicted of or pleaded guilty to any offence listed in ERISA §411 — robbery, bribery, extortion, embezzlement, fraud, grand larceny, burglary, arson, a felony violation of federal or state narcotics law, murder, rape, kidnapping, perjury, assault with intent to kill, any crime involving a violation of ERISA Title I or II, or conspiracy or attempt to commit any of these.
Ask separately whether they are subject to any court order, regulatory bar or professional disciplinary finding that would prevent service as a fiduciary.
Ask for disclosure of outside directorships, business interests and related-party relationships that could conflict with the exclusive-benefit duty under ERISA §404(a)(1)(A).
Require the attestation to be signed before appointment and to state that a false answer is grounds for immediate removal.
File the executed attestation in iManage and record the signature date on the appointment task.
checklist.done: a signed, dated attestation covering the §411 offence list, regulatory bars and conflicts is on file before appointment.

checklist.step: Assess the returned report against the §411 offence list
actions: Read the vendor report yourself rather than accepting the vendor's clear/consider flag, which is set to a generic adjudication matrix and not to ERISA §411.
For every conviction or guilty plea found, identify the offence, the jurisdiction, the conviction date and the date of the end of imprisonment where applicable.

Compute the bar period: thirteen years from the later of the conviction date or the end of imprisonment, unless the sentencing court set a shorter period or the individual obtained a determination from the US Parole Commission or the sentencing court.
Match the offence to the §411 list on its elements rather than its local name, since state offence titles vary and a plea to a lesser included offence may still be within the list.
Where the match is arguable, obtain the court disposition record before deciding, not the database summary.
checklist.done: each finding has an offence-element analysis, a computed bar end date and, where arguable, the underlying court disposition record on file.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA pre-adverse and adverse action sequence where a finding blocks appointment
actions: Send the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the CFPB Summary of Your Rights Under the FCRA before any decision is communicated.
Allow a reasonable period — the working standard is 5 business days — for the individual to dispute accuracy or provide context, and record what they provide.
Where the individual disputes the record, hold the decision until the vendor's reinvestigation completes and read the corrected report.

Where the decision stands, issue the adverse action notice naming the consumer reporting agency, stating the agency did not make the decision, and setting out the right to a free report and to dispute.
Record the notice dates and the individual's response in the determination file, since the process is the defensible part.
checklist.done: the pre-adverse notice with report and rights summary, the response window, and the adverse action notice are all documented with dates.

checklist.step: Issue the written fitness determination
actions: Write a determination memo per appointment stating the role, its ERISA flag, the searches performed and their coverage period, the findings, the §411 analysis and the conclusion — eligible, ineligible until a stated date, or eligible with conditions.
Where the conclusion is eligible with conditions, name the conditions (no sole signing authority, no trust wire authority, additional supervision) and the person accountable for enforcing them.
Sign and date the memo within 3 business days of receiving the complete report and file it in iManage under the appointment reference.
Notify the Corporate Secretary of the outcome so the appointment resolution proceeds or is withdrawn, and notify Compliance so the fidelity bond schedule can be updated.
Never allow a provisional or verbal clearance — an appointment resolution passed on a verbal clearance is unsupported.
checklist.done: a signed, dated determination memo with a stated conclusion and any conditions is on file within 3 business days of the complete report.

checklist.step: Complete the appointment only after the determination
actions: Confirm the determination memo reference and date before drafting the appointment resolution, and record the reference in the resolution.
Confirm the appointee signs the fiduciary acceptance letter after the determination date, so the sequence is screen, determine, appoint, accept.
Update the fiduciary register with the determination date alongside the appointment and acceptance dates.
Where an individual has already begun acting before the determination completed, stop them acting, escalate to General Counsel for a ratification opinion, and log the breach.
Give Compliance the new appointee's funds-handling status so the ERISA §412 bond schedule is re-sized within 30 days if needed.
checklist.done: every appointment resolution cites a determination memo dated before it, and the acceptance letter is signed after the determination date.

checklist.step: Extend the assessment to key service provider personnel
actions: Identify service providers whose staff act as fiduciaries or handle plan funds — the recordkeeper's trust operations, the TPA's claims appeal deciders, the custodian's payment authorisers.
Require in the contract that the provider screens those personnel against ERISA §411 and bonds them, and obtain the provider's annual written confirmation naming the standard applied.
Where the provider's own bond is relied on to satisfy ERISA §412, obtain the bond and confirm the plan is a named insured and the coverage level meets the 10%-of-funds-handled test.
Record the provider confirmations in the vendor file as part of the prudent-monitoring evidence required by ERISA §404(a)(1)(B) and §404(e).
Escalate any provider that will not confirm to the ERISA Plan Administration Committee as a retention decision.
checklist.done: each provider whose staff act as fiduciaries or handle funds has a current written §411 screening confirmation and a validated bond on the vendor file.

checklist.step: Run the annual incumbent re-attestation
actions: Generate the incumbent population from the HRIS ERISA flags plus the fiduciary and delegation registers, and reconcile the two lists before launching.

Launch the attestation campaign 45 days before plan year end asking each incumbent to reconfirm the §411 position, any new regulatory bar or disciplinary finding, and any new conflict or outside directorship since the last attestation.
Chase non-responders at 30, 14 and 3 days, then escalate to the incumbent's committee chair; a non-response is not a clean attestation.
Refer every positive disclosure to Employment Counsel for a fresh determination within 3 business days.
Re-screen incumbents in the highest-risk funds-handling roles on a rolling three-year cycle rather than relying only on self-attestation.
checklist.done: 100% of incumbents have a dated attestation or an escalation on file by plan year end, with every positive disclosure referred for a fresh determination.

checklist.step: Reconcile the bonded population to the funds-handling population
actions: Take the ERISA-FUNDS-HANDLER population from the HRIS and compare it to the persons covered by the ERISA §412 fidelity bond schedule.
Confirm the bond covers every handler and that no §411-barred person is covered, since ERISA §412 forbids bonding a person the statute bars.
Recompute the bond amount as 10% of funds handled in the preceding plan year with the statutory floor and caps and confirm the policy meets it.
Where a new handler was appointed mid-year, confirm the schedule was updated within 30 days.
Give the Controller the reconciled figures to support the Form 5500 Schedule H or I bonding answer.
checklist.done: the bonded population equals the funds-handling population with no barred person covered, and the amount supports the Form 5500 bonding answer.

checklist.step: Remove immediately where a bar or a false attestation is found
actions: Where a §411 bar is established for a serving person, remove them from every covered role the same business day and record the exact time authority ended.
Identify every fiduciary act and every plan-asset transaction they touched during the barred period and give the list to the ERISA Plan Administration Committee.
Decide on ratification of valid acts, correction of invalid ones, and whether the EBSA Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program applies to any transaction that harmed plan assets.
Assess and document the self-reporting position to EBSA, since ERISA §411 service is a criminal provision.
Notify the fidelity bond surety, because coverage of a barred person may itself void or restrict cover.
checklist.done: the barred person is removed same day, their acts are listed and dispositioned, and the self-reporting and surety notification positions are documented.

checklist.step: Report the assessment position to the committee
actions: Prepare the quarterly paper: appointments assessed, average days from offer to determination, appointments blocked or conditioned, attestation completion rate, provider confirmations obtained and open exceptions.
Name any person who acted before a determination, what they did, and the ratification position, rather than reporting it as a process metric.
Table bonding reconciliation results and any gap between handlers and bonded persons.
Load the paper to the board portal 5 business days ahead and have the Corporate Secretary minute the Committee's decisions.
Track Committee actions on the governance action log to closure.
checklist.done: the quarterly paper is tabled with 5 business days' notice, names every pre-determination act, and the Committee's decisions are minuted.

checklist.step: Retain and restrict access to the assessment file
actions: File per appointment: the FCRA disclosure and authorisation, the vendor report, the attestation, the determination memo, any pre-adverse and adverse action notices, and the appointment resolution reference.
Apply the 6-year ERISA §107 retention label measured from the end of the appointment, and the FCRA and state record-disposal rules for the consumer report itself.
Restrict access to Employment Counsel and the named HR Business Partner through a repository access group, and log every access, because the file holds criminal-history and consumer-report data.
Index by employee id, plan and appointment date so an EBSA or state examiner request can be answered under a confidentiality request within 10 business days.
Confirm secure disposal at the end of retention using a method that renders the consumer report unreadable, and record the disposal.
checklist.done: each assessment file is retained with the 6-year label under restricted, logged access and is indexed by employee id, plan and appointment date.

testing.step: Build the population of appointments and incumbents
actions: Extract from the HRIS every hire, promotion, transfer and secondment into an ERISA-flagged position in the period, with effective date and prior position.
Extract the incumbent ERISA-flagged population at period end and the fiduciary and delegation registers, and reconcile the three lists person by person.
Add director appointments from the board portal and key service provider personnel from the vendor files.
Investigate every person appearing on a register but not carrying an HRIS ERISA flag — an untagged fiduciary never hits the screening gate and is the core failure mode.
Sign the population as complete with the queries, run date and counts.
testing.done: the appointment and incumbent populations reconcile across the HRIS, the fiduciary and delegation registers and the board portal, and untagged fiduciaries are listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the role map to plan documents and functional reality
actions: Read the plan documents, delegation instruments and the claims procedure and list the functions that carry discretionary authority or funds handling.
Compare that list to the HRIS ERISA flags and identify any function performed by an unflagged position.
Test functional fiduciary status rather than title — anyone who in practice decides appeals, authorises a trust payment or selects an investment option is a fiduciary regardless of the map.
Treat every unmapped fiduciary function as a Critical scope exception, ranking above any individual screening failure.
testing.done: every discretionary or funds-handling function in the plan documents maps to a flagged position, or a Critical scope exception is raised.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of appointments
actions: Take 100% of appointments to plan committee, trustee, appeals-decider and trust-payment-authority roles, and 100% of director appointments.
Take 20 further appointments by seeded random selection across the remaining ERISA-flagged population, weighted to internal promotions.
Take 25 incumbents at random from the annual attestation population.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample re-draws identically, and reference individuals by employee id only in the workpaper.
Confirm the auditor processed none of the sampled appointments.
testing.done: the sample is drawn and reproducible, covers all high-authority appointments, and identifies individuals by employee id only.

testing.step: Recompute the sequence of screen, determine, appoint and act
actions: For each sampled appointment, list four dates from source: authorisation signed, vendor report received, determination memo signed and appointment resolution passed.
Confirm the order is strictly increasing; any determination dated after the resolution is a Critical exception.

Compare the determination date to the individual's first recorded fiduciary act — a committee vote, an appeal decision, a payment authorisation — taken from minutes, the claims platform or the trust payment log rather than the HRIS.
Recompute the days from complete report to determination against the 3-business-day standard and from offer to screening order against the 2-business-day standard.
Treat any fiduciary act before the determination date as an unauthorised act and refer it for a ratification opinion.
testing.done: each sampled appointment has a four-date sequence proved from source and the first fiduciary act tested against the determination date.

testing.step: Re-perform the §411 analysis on findings
actions: Take every sampled appointment whose vendor report returned a record and read the underlying court disposition rather than the database summary.
Independently match the offence elements to the ERISA §411 list and recompute the thirteen-year bar from the later of conviction date or end of imprisonment.
Compare your conclusion to the determination memo; a right conclusion reached without an element analysis is still an exception because the process is what defends it.
Confirm any shortened bar relied on is supported by a sentencing court statement or a US Parole Commission determination on file, not by assertion.
Confirm no person with an unexpired bar appears anywhere in the fiduciary register, the funds-handler list or the fidelity bond schedule.
testing.done: each finding has an independent element analysis and recomputed bar date, with any shortened bar supported by a court or Parole Commission record.

testing.step: Test the FCRA process evidence
actions: Confirm the disclosure document for each sampled appointment is standalone, with no liability waiver or extraneous text, and that the authorisation is signed and dated before the search order date.
For appointments blocked or conditioned on a finding, confirm the pre-adverse notice enclosed the report and the CFPB rights summary and pre-dated the decision by a reasonable period.
Confirm the adverse action notice names the consumer reporting agency, states the agency did not make the decision, and sets out the dispute and free-report rights.
Confirm any dispute was held open until the vendor reinvestigation completed and the corrected report was read before the final decision.
testing.done: every sampled appointment shows a standalone disclosure signed before the search and, where adverse, a complete and correctly sequenced FCRA notice trail.

testing.step: Reconcile attestations across the full incumbent population
actions: Match the attestation campaign responses to the incumbent population person by person and compute the completion rate against the 100% standard.
Confirm every non-responder was escalated to their committee chair and that no non-response was closed as complete.
Read every positive disclosure and confirm it was referred to Employment Counsel within 3 business days and that a fresh determination exists.
Confirm the rolling three-year re-screen actually ran for the highest-risk funds-handling incumbents due in the period.
List any incumbent with no attestation and no escalation as a Critical exception.
testing.done: the attestation population reconciles to incumbents with a computed completion rate, every positive disclosure has a fresh determination, and gaps are listed.

testing.step: Reconcile funds handlers to the fidelity bond schedule
actions: Compare the ERISA-FUNDS-HANDLER population to the persons or positions covered by the fidelity bond and list anyone handling funds who is not covered.
Confirm no person with an unexpired §411 bar is covered by the bond, since bonding a barred person is itself a statutory breach.
Recompute the bond amount as 10% of funds handled with the statutory floor and caps and compare to the policy in force.
Confirm mid-year appointments were reflected in the schedule within 30 days and compare the result to the Form 5500 Schedule H or I bonding answer.
testing.done: every funds handler is bonded, no barred person is covered, and the recomputed bond amount ties to the policy and the Form 5500 answer.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception referencing the employee id, role, plan and the specific control that failed.

Assign a root cause — role never flagged in the HRIS, gate bypassed on an internal move, vendor pack missing federal search, determination made on the vendor flag rather than an element analysis, attestation non-response closed as complete, handler not added to the bond — and a named owner.
Set 30 days for scope, gating and bonding failures and 90 days for systemic process or system changes, with closure evidence stated up front.
Refer every act taken before a determination to General Counsel for a ratification opinion and, where plan assets moved, a Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with a root cause, a named owner, a dated remediation and, for pre-determination acts, a counsel referral.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Count the zero-tolerance failures — persons acting with no completed determination, any §411-barred person in a covered role or on the bond, and any incumbent without an attestation at plan year end.
Compute the attestation completion rate and the average offer-to-determination and report-to-determination day counts.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind every figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside HR and Legal and processed none of the sampled appointments, sign the workpaper.

Report to the ERISA Plan Administration Committee and the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Fitness and Propriety / <quarter> with the 6-year label and restricted access.
testing.done: a signed workpaper counting zero-tolerance failures, stating attestation completion and a conclusion, is filed under restricted access with committee reporting dates.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual cycle that puts every ERISA governance policy in front of the Board or the ERISA Plan Administration Committee for review and approval — the fiduciary governance policy, the investment policy statement, the service provider selection and monitoring policy, the claims procedure policy, the cybersecurity program policy and the ERISA record retention policy.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — ERISA §404(a)(1)(B) prudence and §404(a)(1)(D) plan-document compliance, §404(e) prudent selection and monitoring of service providers, 29 CFR 2560.503-1(b) written claims procedures described in the SPD, 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c) covered service provider disclosures, 29 CFR 2578.1 abandoned-plan procedures, and the EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices (2021) and Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01, each re-read on dol.gov and eCFR at the start of the annual review.

In-scope processes.value: Annual policy inventory, gap assessment against current regulatory text, drafting and redlining, functional and legal review, committee recommendation, Board approval, publication to the workforce and service providers, and the exception process for any deviation from an approved policy.

In-scope systems.value: Policy inventory, review calendar, redlines, recommendation papers, resolutions and approved minutes held in the board portal; approved policy editions published to Microsoft 365 / SharePoint for the workforce with acknowledgement tracking in the learning management system.

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Governance Policy Review Procedure — the policy inventory with owners and approval bodies, the annual calendar spreading policies across the four committee sittings, the mandatory gap assessment against current regulatory text, the redline and review sequence, the Board approval and minuting standard, and the publication and attestation rules.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board on the recommendation of the ERISA Plan Administration Committee; re-approved annually, and the procedure itself is one of the policies in the inventory so it cannot escape its own cycle.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual per policy: gap assessment complete 90 days before the target sitting, redline and legal review complete 45 days before, committee recommendation 30 days before, papers to the board portal 5 business days before, Board approval within 12 months of the last approval, publication within 10 business days of approval and workforce acknowledgement within 30 days of publication.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal calendar drives the policy review calendar with owner reminders at 120, 90, 45 and 10 days before the target sitting; a hard alert to the Board Governance Lead and General Counsel at 30 days before any policy passes 12 months since its last approval.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each approved policy edition with its effective date, the gap assessment, the redline against the prior edition, the recommendation paper, the approving resolution and minute, and the acknowledgement report, retained 6 years per ERISA §107 and permanently where the policy governed a benefit determination, per ERISA §209.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Policies past their 12-month approval date, approvals granted without a gap assessment, policies published without Board approval and departures from an approved policy in practice are logged as governance issues with owner, due date and closure evidence.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Confirms in writing that each remediated policy edition reflects current regulatory text and that any period in which a plan operated under a lapsed or unapproved policy has been assessed for fiduciary exposure.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every policy on the ERISA governance policy inventory, every approval decision taken by the Board or the ERISA Plan Administration Committee in the year, and the published editions in force across the plan year.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any policy in force with no Board approval in the last 12 months, any approval granted with no documented gap assessment against current regulatory text, and any published edition that differs from the approved edition are fails; workforce acknowledgement must reach 95% of the target population within 30 days of publication.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per policy; the test runs once a year over the full inventory after the last committee sitting of the plan year, with a targeted interim test of any policy amended out of cycle in response to a regulatory change.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in the Corporate Secretariat or own any policy in the inventory, and must not have drafted or presented any sampled recommendation paper.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policy governance test workpaper — inventory reconciliation, approval-date recomputation, gap-assessment trace, published-versus-approved edition comparison and acknowledgement reconciliation — in the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Policy Governance / <plan year>.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Policy evidence pack — the inventory, each approved edition with its effective date, the approving minute and resolution, the gap assessment and the acknowledgement report — producible to an EBSA investigator or a plan auditor within 10 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary assembles the pack; General Counsel is the single channel to EBSA and decides whether a period of operating under a lapsed policy requires disclosure or correction, including through the Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program where plan assets were affected.

checklist.step: Maintain the ERISA governance policy inventory
