testing.step: Re-perform control tests on the sampled effective controls
actions: For each sampled control rated effective, inspect the test evidence and judge whether the test actually exercised the control rather than confirming its configuration existed.

Re-execute at least four tests directly — attempt a cross-plan data read with a standard entitlement, replay a detection test event in Splunk SIEM, re-check the contact centre identity-proofing script against a live call recording, and re-check an interface's TLS configuration.
Compare your result to the recorded effectiveness rating and treat any difference as an exception in the assessment, separate from the underlying control weakness.
Confirm controls rated effective on design alone, with no operating test, are listed as an assessment quality exception.
testing.done: sampled effective ratings are supported by inspected test evidence with at least four tests re-executed and differences listed as assessment exceptions.

testing.step: Verify scan and test coverage against the asset inventory
actions: Reconcile authenticated scan results to the frozen asset inventory and compute the percentage of in-scope assets with a scan in the assessment window.
Confirm scans were authenticated rather than unauthenticated, since an unauthenticated scan understates exposure and is often the reason a clean result is wrong.
Reconcile endpoint agent coverage in CrowdStrike Falcon to the population of workstations with participant-data access.

Confirm the penetration test scope covered the participant portal authentication, account recovery and transaction authorisation paths and the social engineering component, and read the rules of engagement for carve-outs that removed the interesting targets.
List every asset with no scan and every scope carve-out as a coverage exception.
testing.done: scan and endpoint coverage percentages are computed against the frozen inventory, authentication is verified, and penetration test carve-outs are listed.

testing.step: Recompute findings ageing and test closure quality
actions: Recompute days open for every finding from raise date to closure or to test date, and compare against the 30/60/90-day severity windows.
For each sampled closed finding, open the closure evidence and confirm it is a retest result, not a change record or an owner assertion.
For vulnerability closures, confirm a post-fix authenticated scan covering all affected assets shows the finding absent, not a sample.
Confirm Critical and High closures carry the Chief Info Security Officer's signature and that every date extension has a documented fresh exposure assessment and approver.
Treat any finding closed without retest evidence as still open and re-age it from its original raise date.
testing.done: every finding's ageing is recomputed against its severity window and every sampled closure is proved by retest evidence or reopened.

testing.step: Test that risk acceptances were ratified by the plan fiduciary
actions: For each risk acceptance, find the ERISA Plan Administration Committee minute that ratified it and confirm it was presented individually with participants exposed, compensating control and expiry date.
Confirm the minute records a resolution and vote rather than a noting, and that quorum was recorded.
Confirm no acceptance is past its expiry or has been renewed without a fresh exposure assessment.
Treat an acceptance approved only within the technology organisation as a fiduciary governance failure, since residual risk to participant data cannot be accepted below the Committee.
testing.done: every acceptance traces to an individual, quorate Committee ratification with an unexpired date, or is raised as a fiduciary governance failure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the scenario or finding, the system or provider, the participants exposed and the control that failed.

Assign a root cause — asset never in scope, exclusion undocumented, scan unauthenticated, control rated on design only, closure without retest, acceptance not ratified, extension granted without reassessment — and a named owner.
Set 30 days for scope, closure-quality and acceptance exceptions and 90 days for methodology and process changes, with closure evidence stated up front.
Refer any finding that indicates prior participant-data exposure to General Counsel and the Privacy Officer for a disclosure assessment.
Carry every open issue into the quarterly interim test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with root cause, named owner, dated remediation and, where exposure is indicated, a counsel and privacy referral.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Count the zero-tolerance failures — assets excluded without an approved basis, Criticals open past 30 days, Highs past 60 days, closures without retest evidence and unratified acceptances.
Compute scan and control test coverage, the on-time remediation rate by severity and the residual position against Committee tolerance.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind every figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the CISO organisation and owns no finding, sign the workpaper.

Report to the ERISA Plan Administration Committee and the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under ERISA / Cyber Risk Assessment / <plan year> with the 6-year ERISA §107 label.
testing.done: a signed workpaper counting zero-tolerance failures, stating coverage and on-time remediation rates and a conclusion, is filed with Committee reporting dates.
